answer.rationale: Memory_31 and memory_91 show moderate support—they improve activation and engagement but lack evidence of long-term retention or revenue durability. Memory_44 is strongly supported because enterprise sales-assisted flows typically yield higher LTV and stickier accounts. Memory_86 is also strongly supported because faster time-to-value correlates with retention. Memory_73 is weakly supported because promotional pricing in price-sensitive segments risks commoditization and customer quality; no durability signal is reported. Memory_57 is the least supported: referral programs among established customers add revenue but do not address sustainable growth mechanisms, lack retention data, and contain an explicit caveat ('without measurable harm') that masks unknown longer-term effects. For sustainable long-term qualified revenue, customer quality, retention, and LTV matter more than transactional acquisition or promotional velocity.
